STUDY 01 · LANGUAGE MODELS · RELEASED DATA

Homonym Semantics

How does a language model revise an initially plausible interpretation once later context resolves an ambiguous word?

Eight encoder and decoder models · seven homonyms · two senses per word · layerwise hidden-state analysis.

01

Executive summary

  1. We can track meaning.

    Contextual meaning is geometrically traceable as it emerges and changes in model representations.

  2. Meaning is path-dependent.

    An earlier interpretation leaves a measurable trace even after later context requires another meaning.

  3. Interpretation does not start neutral.

    Language models enter ambiguous interpretation with systematic semantic priors.

02

Sense separation, layer by layer

Select a model and word, then scrub through depth. The curve reports the full-space analysis metric; the adjacent cloud is the released display projection of the same 40 profiling sentences at that exact layer.

The marker links the two panels. GDV, adequacy and margins are full-space values; the cloud is a shared-PCA display aid, with every layer standardised separately. View the released geometry export ↗

03

Garden paths versus coherent context

Each pair reaches the same intended meaning at the same analysis layer. One path first makes the other sense plausible; the matched coherent context establishes the intended sense from the start. The map opens from above—drag it to reveal the density depth.

1 prime, 2 homonym, 3 resolver. Depth is the negative density of the 40 profile sentences in the PC1–PC2 plane, scaled so the deepest well is −1: a display aid, not a model energy. X = sense centroid.

04

Revision leaves a decision-boundary cost

Across the released garden-path evaluation, later resolution often succeeds—but not without a measurable remnant of the earlier interpretation.

77.2%of items revise toward the resolving sense
40.3%still retain a path-dependent trace at the resolver
36.9ppdecision-boundary gap between coherent and conflicting contexts

These headline estimates summarize the revision and decision-boundary analyses in the release; the matched trajectories above make the mechanism inspectable item by item.

05

Sticky priors

Before disambiguating context arrives, models already lean toward one sense. Switch between the bare word and ambiguous carrier sentences to see how this starting bias persists across models and homonyms.
